field.label: Enabled
field.help: Block the devices listed. Off, the rules are gone at the next filter reload; the list stays.

field.label: Log blocked packets
field.help: Write every packet the rules block to the firewall log.

field.label: Isolate devices that reach a command-and-control list
field.help: When os-netreport records that a device of your networks tried to reach an address on a command-and-control list that os-blocklists blocks, the device is isolated by its MAC address for the time below: the firewall blocks the addresses it is seen with, both ways, and cuts their open connections; an address it takes later is blocked from the next check, within a minute. Checked every minute, for connections in the last 10 minutes. The device is the one the ARP or NDP table shows at the address that reached the list, or the one os-netreport names where they show none. Never the firewall itself, its gateways, its HA peer's addresses set under High Availability, an address logged in to its web GUI or SSH, or an address this page was opened from in the last 7 days. A MAC address the ARP table shows with more than one IPv4 address at the time is isolated by the addresses that reached the list only; a router that translates addresses shows one, and is isolated with every device behind it. Isolation is at the firewall: devices on the same switch still reach each other. Separate from the list of blocked devices and from Enabled above. Off by default.

field.label: Isolation time (hours)
field.help: How long a device stays isolated, from 1 to 720 hours; a shorter time set ends the isolations already running sooner. Undo on the Isolated devices tab lets a device go at once, and holds until its isolation would have ended.
